headline: Growth reaccelerates, margins turn positive, guidance raised
summary_short: CrowdStrike's press release reports total revenue of $1.39B, up 26% year-over-year, with GAAP net income of $27.8M reversing a $104.3M loss a year earlier and record free cash flow of $468.5M.
summary_long: Revenue rose 26% y/y to $1.39B on subscription growth and record net new ARR of $256M (ARR +24% y/y to $5.51B). GAAP operating loss narrowed to $30.6M from $118.7M as revenue outgrew opex; non-GAAP operating income rose to $325.7M from $201.1M. Net income swung to $27.8M from a $104.3M loss, aided by a $36.4M strategic-investment gain; GAAP diluted EPS was $0.11 versus -$0.42 (pre-split). Cash fell to $4.55B from $5.23B after an $881.4M acquisition, alongside record operating cash flow ($590.9M) and free cash flow ($468.5M). CrowdStrike raised FY27 net new ARR growth guidance to 27.7% at the midpoint (+520bp) and announced a four-for-one stock split effective July 2026.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes growth to record net new ARR of $256M (+32% y/y), platform adoption from existing customers, new-logo lands, and increased partner engagement.
Subscription gross margin expanded because subscription revenue (+26% y/y) grew faster than subscription cost of revenue (+19.5% y/y); not separately explained in the release.
GAAP operating loss narrowed as total revenue grew 26% y/y while total operating expenses rose only 15% y/y; not separately explained in the release.
Swing to profit reflects the narrower operating loss plus a $36.4M gain on strategic investments and a $10.8M deferred-tax benefit, both disclosed in the GAAP statements.

CFO cites 'record Q2 pipeline, continued strong retention, Falcon Flex momentum, and the AI technology wave' as the basis for raising full-year net new ARR growth guidance to 27.7% at the midpoint.
